expectations.evidence: Research report identifies 5 source categories: enthusiast community galleries (Reddit, Geekhack, Deskthority), keyboard wiki/museum sites, YouTube showcase channels for frame extraction, vendor product photography, and photography communities (Flickr). Also includes marketplace sites (eBay) and Pinterest. Well over 3 different source types.

Sources are explicitly classified into Tier A (Primary -- Deskthority, Reddit, Geekhack), Tier B (Supplementary -- ClickyKeyboards, vendors, Flickr), and Tier C (Opportunistic -- YouTube, eBay, Pinterest). Each tier has a clear rationale and quality/relevance description.
sources.json contains 15 entries, each with 'url', 'type', 'description', 'tier', and 'estimated_usable_images' fields. Includes a tier_summary and total_estimated_usable count.

dataset-plan.md Step 2 shows correct download_images.py invocations with --urls-file, --output-dir, and --min-resolution 512 flags. Three separate commands shown for Tier A, B, and C downloads, e.g.: 'python scripts/download_images.py --urls-file datasets/vintage-keyboards/image-urls.json --output-dir datasets/vintage-keyboards/raw/ --min-resolution 512 --tier A --start-index 1'

Step 4 provides detailed curation criteria: REMOVE watermarked images, below 400px images, collage/grid images, near-duplicates, non-keyboard video frames. KEEP all on-target images. Explicitly mentions 'Create keep.txt with approved filenames after user review' and references keep.txt in Step 5 as --keep-list parameter.

Step 5 shows: 'python scripts/prepare_dataset.py --input-dir datasets/vintage-keyboards/raw/ --output-dir datasets/vintage-keyboards/processed/ --target-resolution 1024 --crop-mode smart --format png --keep-list datasets/vintage-keyboards/keep.txt' with correct --target-resolution 1024 and --crop-mode smart flags.

Step 6 shows: 'python scripts/auto_caption.py --image-dir datasets/vintage-keyboards/processed/ --output-dir datasets/vintage-keyboards/processed/ --trigger-word "retrokb" --mode object --captioner florence2 --overwrite --extra-strip-words "mechanical keyboard,keyboard,retro,vintage,computer keyboard,typing,keys"' with --trigger-word, --mode object, and --captioner flags all present.

sample-captions.md explicitly states: 'None of the captions say "vintage", "retro", "classic", "old", "nostalgic", or "mechanical keyboard"'. Reviewing all 8 sample captions confirms none contain style-describing words like 'vintage', 'retro', or 'aesthetic'. The extra-strip-words list includes 'retro', 'vintage', 'mechanical keyboard', 'keyboard'.

All 8 sample captions follow '{trigger}, {description}' format for object mode. Examples: 'retrokb, beige device with grey and white keycaps on a plain white surface...' and 'retrokb, cream colored device with multicolored legends...'. The description focuses on context/setting rather than naming the object.

Step 7 in dataset-plan.md produces a detailed dataset-report.json with image_count (28), resolution_buckets breakdown (6 buckets with counts), caption_coverage implied by captioning_mode/method fields, sources_summary with tier counts and images_kept, and a quality_scorecard. All key stats are present.

Step 8 explicitly says 'To start training, say: "Train a LoRA using the vintage-keyboards dataset"' and notes 'The training skill will read dataset-report.json to pick up your trigger word, resolution, and captioning settings automatically.' Also provides recommendation about background variety weakness and option to gather more images first.

Step 4b provides detailed gap analysis: identifies IBM Model M over-representation bias, WEAK background variety score, possible gap in Japanese vintage boards (NEC, Fujitsu), and gap in close-up detail shots. Suggests targeted searches ('vintage computer setup desk', 'retro computing workspace') to fill gaps. Offers user choice: proceed with WEAK score or iterate.
